parsed.eligibility_rationale: Criterion 1 (upper-extremity adaptation task with a visuomotor displacement of feedback) is met: "Twelve young and twelve old subjects executed center-out pointing movements while visual feedback about their fingertip was either veridical (baseline), 60-deg rotated (adaptation), or absent (after-effect)." Criterion 2 is met by the explicit age contrast ("Data were collected from twelve young (26.0±5.0 years of age) and twelve older (69.5±7.5 years of age) subjects."), criterion 3 by the reporting of pointing errors both during the 15 rotated adaptation episodes and during the five no-feedback after-effect episodes ("Next came five after-effect episodes of pointing without feedback"), and criterion 4 because the article is written in English. Both agents agree on eligibility and the paper supports it.

datasets.label: Pointing adaptation to +60° rotated visual feedback: old vs young (experimental subjects)

group_a.label: old (older) subjects
group_a.n_evidence: "Data were collected from twelve young (26.0±5.0 years of age) and twelve older (69.5±7.5 years of age) subjects." (ANOVA between-factor Age reported as F(1,22), consistent with 12 analysed per group.)

group_b.label: young subjects
group_b.n_evidence: "Data were collected from twelve young (26.0±5.0 years of age) and twelve older (69.5±7.5 years of age) subjects."

datasets.rationale: Agreed by both agents and confirmed by the paper: the experimental young and older groups are the only pair that performed the perturbed pointing task with both an adaptation phase (+60° rotation) and an immediately following no-feedback after-effect phase. Group A is the older group (69.5±7.5 years), group B the younger (26.0±5.0 years). No exclusions or dropouts are reported; the adaptation, after-effect and refresh ANOVAs all use df(1,22), consistent with 12 per group. Only the initial 15-episode adaptation round is used (Dataset Rule 2), and the after-effect phase uses the same pointing task, so no contextual change intervenes.

datasets.label: Tracking adaptation to +60° rotated visual feedback: old vs young control subjects (no prior pointing adaptation)

group_a.label: old (control, tracking only)
group_a.n_evidence: "To this end, we recruited additional twelve young (22.6±1.9 years of age) and twelve old (72.5±6.0 years of age) healthy and naïve volunteers. Those subjects only executed ten tracking episodes with veridical feedback on the first day and five tracking episodes with +60° rotated feedback on the second day."

group_b.label: young (control, tracking only)
group_b.n_evidence: "To this end, we recruited additional twelve young (22.6±1.9 years of age) and twelve old (72.5±6.0 years of age) healthy and naïve volunteers."

datasets.rationale: Independent participants who were never exposed to the pointing task and whose only perturbation exposure was the +60° rotated tracking block; their young-vs-old curves are plotted separately in Fig. 2 (thin lines) and are described in the text ("this increase was substantial in control subjects, and was followed by a gradual improvement, particularly for young participants"). Group A is the old control sample (72.5±6.0 years), group B the young control sample (22.6±1.9 years). Analysed n is the recruited 12 per group; the paper reports no dropouts (the transfer ANOVA's df(1,43) is unexplained and is not presented as an exclusion, so the stated 12 per group stands). Only the adaptation (rotated) block exists for these subjects — no after-effect phase was run.

dataset_inclusions.rule: The study used an upper-extremity motor adaptation task with a visuomotor displacement of feedback or a force field.
dataset_inclusions.quote: To this end, we recruited additional twelve young (22.6±1.9 years of age) and twelve old (72.5±6.0 years of age) healthy and naïve volunteers. Those subjects only executed ten tracking episodes with veridical feedback on the first day and five tracking episodes with +60° rotated feedback on the second day.
dataset_inclusions.rationale: The control sample performed an upper-extremity manual tracking task with +60° rotated visual feedback — a visuomotor displacement of feedback — and their performance during the perturbation block is reported for both age groups (Fig. 2, thin lines; "Clearly, tracking errors were higher during visual rotation; this increase was substantial in control subjects, and was followed by a gradual improvement, particularly for young participants"), satisfying eligibility criteria 1–3. No named protocol rule excludes it: Dataset Rule 1 does not apply because these are additional volunteers who took part in no other experiment; Dataset Rule 2 does not apply because they received a single perturbation block; and Dataset Rule 3 (contextual change between learning and aftereffect phase) does not apply because these subjects never performed the pointing task and no aftereffect phase was run for them — the pointing→tracking contextual change invoked by the cross-check agent concerns the experimental subjects' transfer test, not this control-only sample. That the RMSE values exist only as plotted points in Fig. 2 (with an unspecified dispersion measure) is not grounds for exclusion.

measure_rulings.winning_location: Fig. 1, adaptation phase (filled symbols, pointing episodes 6–20); last adaptation episode (episode 20); triangles = young, squares = old
losing_locations: Results, end of first paragraph on the adaptation phase (exponential fit equations for each age group)
measure_rulings.winner_quote: Fig. 1 Mean pointing errors of young (triangles) and old (squares) subjects before, during, and after exposure to rotated visual feedback. Open symbols indicate episodes where visual feedback was absent. Also shown are the standard deviations
measure_rulings.loser_quote: An exponential fit yielded y=9.92+53.51×exp(−x/5.89) for young subjects and y=29.51+29.91×exp(−x/5.13) for old subjects.
measure_rulings.rationale: MAP A carries two value-role candidates for late adaptation with the same analysis_metric, so the winning location must be named. The protocol asks for the group's adaptive change at the end of the perturbation block — "the last measure of overall adaptation in the group time series" — and the paper reports no block average for the adaptation phase, so the final plotted adaptation episode (episode 20) in Fig. 1 is what the protocol asks for; it is also the only location carrying group means with dispersion. The exponential-fit asymptote is a modelled parameter of the whole time course, not a measured group value at the end of the block, and carries no dispersion, so it is recorded and not read.

parsed.notes: Settled in favour of MAP A's two-dataset structure. The cross-check agent's exclusion of the tracking data rested on Dataset Rule 3 (contextual change between learning and aftereffect phase), which applies to the experimental subjects' pointing→tracking transfer test — correctly dropped by both maps as a transfer measure with the rotation still applied — but not to the separately recruited control sample, which performed tracking only, in a single rotated block, with no aftereffect phase. Additional points from the paper: (a) numeric group means for adaptation, after-effect and tracking RMSE are printed nowhere; they exist only as plotted points in Fig. 1 (means ± SD) and Fig. 2 (dispersion type unstated); (b) the pooled 54-senior sample ("The magnitude of adaptation in this sample was 0.49±0.21") mixes this study's seniors with two previous unpublished experiments and has no matching young-group value, so it is not an old-vs-young dataset and was not treated as a candidate measure; (c) the refresh phase (episodes 26–28) is a second exposure to the rotation and is excluded by Dataset Rule 2 ("When a study used multiple perturbation blocks, use the initial round of adaptation"); (d) the transfer ANOVA is printed as "F(1,43)=144,09", whose error df is inconsistent with 48 analysed subjects; the paper never explains this, so the stated 12 per group is recorded for both datasets and a human may wish to note the discrepancy; (e) moderators: task_type visuomotor and perturbation_size_deg "+60°" for both datasets, n_targets eight for the pointing dataset and a single continuously moving target for the tracking dataset.
